books.title: Protocols of Shadow
books.subtitle: The Onyx Hand Internal Codex
books.author: Judge Obsidian
books.description: A black leather tome with no visible title on its spine. The pages are thin as onion skin and whisper when turned.

content.text: PROTOCOLS OF SHADOW
Internal Codex of the Onyx Hand
Compiled by Judge Obsidian
For Initiates of the Third Circle and Above

You hold in your hands a document that does not exist. The Onyx Hand keeps no records. We leave no traces. We cast no shadows — for we ARE the shadow. If you are reading this, you have either earned our trust through years of service, or you have made a very grave mistake.

The protocols contained herein govern our operations, our tribunals, and our sacred duty to maintain balance in a kingdom that has forgotten what balance means. We are not criminals, though the surface world names us such. We are the necessary darkness that defines the light.
"In the absence of justice, we provide order. In the absence of order, we provide consequences."
content.attribution: — The First Judge, founding declaration, 1015 BF

chapters.title: Chapter I: Structure of the Hand

content.text: Chapter I
content.subtitle: Structure of the Hand

content.text: he Onyx Hand operates through a system of concentric circles, each with its own responsibilities, privileges, and — most importantly — limitations on knowledge. What you know depends on where you stand. This is not cruelty; it is protection. The less you know, the less you can betray.

The outermost circle — the First — comprises our eyes and ears. Informants, merchants, beggars, servants. They do not know they serve us. They simply... talk. And we listen. Every tavern conversation, every pillow whisper, every drunken confession flows upward through channels they cannot see.

The Second Circle consists of our hands — the operatives who act upon gathered intelligence. Thieves, smugglers, enforcers. They know they serve the Hand, but they do not know who gives the orders. They receive instructions through dead drops, coded messages, anonymous couriers. They are skilled, loyal, and utterly expendable.

content.title: THE FIVE CIRCLES
entries: First Circle: Unknowing informants and assets
Second Circle: Field operatives and enforcers
Third Circle: Cell leaders and regional coordinators
Fourth Circle: The Tribunal — judges who dispense shadow justice
Fifth Circle: [REDACTED] — existence unconfirmed

content.text: You, initiate, have been elevated to the Third Circle. You will coordinate operations within your assigned territory. You will never meet your counterparts. You will never know how many of us exist. You will report to a voice through a speaking stone, and you will obey without question.

The Fourth Circle comprises the Tribunal — the judges who hear cases that the surface world cannot or will not adjudicate. When the Mages' Guild demands internal arbitration for a murderer, when the Iron Legion's soldiers commit atrocities without consequence, when the powerful crush the weak with impunity... the Tribunal provides an alternative.

Our justice is not gentle. It is not forgiving. But it is FAIR. The Tribunal weighs evidence without regard for wealth, faction, or species. A koopa stands equal to a toad in our courts. A mage's arcane credentials carry no weight against a farmer's honest testimony.

content.label: [ A page has been folded and sealed with black wax. Break the seal → ]

hidden_content.text: The Fifth Circle exists. I have seen the chamber beneath the chamber. Five thrones, five figures, faces hidden even from the Tribunal. They do not judge — they DECIDE. Wars have ended because they willed it. Factions have risen and fallen at their word. I do not know their names. I do not know if they are mortal. I know only that they have watched this kingdom since before the Princess died, and they will watch it long after we are dust. — J.O.

content.text: As a Third Circle operative, you may petition the Tribunal on behalf of those who cannot reach us through normal channels. This is a sacred responsibility. Abuse it, and you will discover that our justice applies to our own as readily as to outsiders.

chapters.title: Chapter II: The Archie Miser Precedent

content.text: Chapter II
content.subtitle: The Archie Miser Precedent

content.text: n Highsun 2, 1040 BF, the Tribunal rendered a verdict that would reshape our relationship with every major faction in the kingdom. The case of Archie Miser — a mage who killed a fellow practitioner — tested the boundaries of our authority and exposed the rot at the heart of the Mages' Guild.

The facts were these: Archie Miser, a human mage of considerable but undisciplined power, engaged in lethal combat with a Guild-credentialed practitioner named Valorian Stormweave. The confrontation occurred in a public market. Seven bystanders were injured. Stormweave died from a combination of fire damage and blunt force trauma when Archie threw him through a load-bearing wall.

The Mages' Guild demanded Archie be surrendered to their internal courts — courts notorious for protecting their own at the expense of outsiders. They cited ancient charter rights. They threatened economic sanctions. They hinted at arcane retaliation.
We told them no.

The trial lasted six hours. Twenty-three witnesses testified. Evidence included scrying reconstructions, physical artifacts, and testimony from two of the injured bystanders. The Tribunal — three judges whose identities remain protected — deliberated for forty-seven minutes before rendering their verdict.
"The killing of Valorian Stormweave constitutes justifiable magical defense. The deceased initiated hostilities with lethal intent. The defendant responded with proportionate force. ACQUITTED."

The Guild's response was immediate and furious. Three observers walked out during the verdict reading. One — a senior enforcer named Magistrix Vellum — was later found dead in her quarters, cause of death listed as 'spontaneous arcane feedback.' The Guild blamed us. We had nothing to do with it.

content.label: [ A notation in different handwriting appears in the margin. Examine it → ]

hidden_content.text: We had EVERYTHING to do with it. Vellum was preparing to expose the Tribunal's location to Guild strike teams. The Fifth Circle authorized her elimination. I was the one who modified her focusing crystal to overload. May her soul find whatever peace awaits oath-breakers. — Agent Whisper

content.text: The Archie Miser case established several crucial precedents:

items.text: The Onyx Hand Tribunal has jurisdiction over any crime committed within unaligned territory, regardless of the perpetrator's factional affiliation.
Guild charter rights do not supersede universal principles of self-defense.
Economic and arcane threats will not influence Tribunal verdicts.
Those who attempt to subvert our justice will face consequences.

content.text: Archie Miser walked free. He has since become a chaos agent of significant concern — his actions aboard the Vigilance and at Raventree Manor have killed dozens. Some within our ranks question whether the acquittal was wise. But wisdom was never the point. JUSTICE was the point. And justice, unlike wisdom, does not concern itself with consequences.
Chapter III
content.subtitle: The Vampire Question

content.text: ithin our ranks, a transformation is occurring that demands acknowledgment. The Onyx Knights — our elite enforcement arm — have increasingly turned to vampirism as a means of enhancing their capabilities. This document will address the theological, practical, and strategic implications of this development.

Let us be clear: the Onyx Hand does not officially sanction vampirism. We do not recruit vampires. We do not create vampires. What we DO acknowledge is that certain operatives, in pursuit of their duties, have accepted the dark gift from sources outside our organization. These operatives retain their positions so long as they adhere to strict protocols.

content.title: VAMPIRE OPERATIVE PROTOCOLS
entries: Feeding is permitted only from willing donors or condemned criminals
Creation of new vampires requires Fifth Circle authorization
Sustaining crystals must be registered with regional coordinators
Daylight operations require specialized equipment and advance notice
Failure to control blood hunger results in immediate termination

content.text: The advantages are undeniable. Vampire operatives possess enhanced strength, speed, and sensory capabilities. They do not age. They can survive injuries that would kill mortal agents ten times over. In a war of shadows, such advantages matter.

The risks, however, are equally significant. Vampires require sustenance that creates dependencies and vulnerabilities. Their aversion to sunlight limits operational flexibility. And the psychological changes that accompany the transformation — the hunger, the detachment from mortal concerns, the gradual erosion of empathy — can compromise an operative's judgment.

Recent events at Raventree Manor have thrown these concerns into sharp relief. Our vampire knights established a nest within the manor, using dark crystals to sustain their undeath and coordinate operations against multiple factions. The strategy was sound. The execution was flawless. And then everything went wrong.

A battle plan discovered by the prisoner Remi detailed an assault strategy to destroy the sustaining crystals and eliminate our knights. The plan originated with Green T of the Tea Leaf Syndicate — an organization we had considered neutralized. Their survival, and their knowledge of our crystal network, suggests a security breach of concerning proportions.

content.label: [ Blood stains obscure part of this page. Carefully clean them to read → ]

hidden_content.text: Knight-Captain Sanguine's final report, recovered from Raventree: 'They know about the crystals. They know about the Fifth Circle. Someone inside the Hand is feeding them information. I am compiling a list of suspects but I fear I will not survive to—' The report ends here. Sanguine's ashes were found scattered across three rooms. We have a traitor. — J.O.

content.text: Until the traitor is identified and eliminated, all vampire operations are suspended. Sustaining crystals are to be relocated to secondary sites. Knight-operatives are to operate independently, without coordination through normal channels. Trust no one. Suspect everyone.
Chapter IV
content.subtitle: The Coming Storm

content.text: ntelligence gathered over the past season paints a picture of converging catastrophes. The planar fractures at Raventree Manor are not an isolated phenomenon — they are symptoms of a deeper instability that threatens the fabric of reality itself. The Oracle is dead. The parallel entities multiply. And Fawful has allied with dragons.
The Fifth Circle has issued a rare directive: all resources are to be redirected toward intelligence gathering on three priority targets.

factions.name: Fawful's Dragon Alliance
factions.description: The mad tactician has somehow brokered an alliance with the remaining dragon flights. After the death of Ignis, the dragons were expected to retreat further into isolation. Instead, they have found a champion willing to wage war on their behalf. Fawful commands strategic brilliance and bottomless spite. The dragons command fire that can melt fortress walls. Together, they pose an existential threat.

factions.name: The Mages' Guild Extraction Team
factions.description: Guild operatives are preparing to extract the ghosts from Raventree Manor — regardless of the cost to the living or the stability of the planar fractures. Their motives remain unclear. The ghosts may contain knowledge, power, or something else entirely. What is clear is that the extraction will cause massive collateral damage, and the Guild considers this acceptable.

factions.name: The Parallel Dan Anomaly
factions.description: Dan the Toad exists in two places simultaneously. The original is held in a Mages' Guild null cage. The parallel walks free, disrupting the Oracle's function and destabilizing local reality. The Guild wants him dead. The Loyalists want him protected. We want to understand what he IS — because whatever created him may be capable of creating more.

content.text: The Fifth Circle's analysis suggests these three threats are connected. Fawful's timing — allying with dragons immediately after Ignis's death — implies foreknowledge. The Guild's urgency regarding Raventree extraction suggests they know something about the planar fractures that they are not sharing. And Dan's existence may be neither accident nor experiment, but the first sign of a larger phenomenon.

Our working theory: someone or something is deliberately destabilizing reality in preparation for a larger event. The assassination of Princess Peach eighty-five years ago may have been the first move in a game we are only now beginning to perceive.

events.event: Princess Peach assassinated through impossible means
Star Road network destroyed — coincidence or preparation?
Onyx Hand founded — were we created to serve this pattern?
Iron Legion consolidates — another prepared piece?
Convergence at Raventree — the endgame begins?

content.text: If this pattern holds, we are not players in this game. We are pieces. And pieces do not get to choose their moves.
Unless they learn the rules.
Appendix
content.subtitle: Operational Cipher Keys — Third Circle Access

content.text: The following cipher is used for all Third Circle communications. Memorize it. This page will be removed and destroyed within 24 hours of your reading.

content.title: COMMUNICATION CIPHER TEST
content.description: Decode the following message to confirm your understanding of the shadow-shift cipher. Each letter is replaced by the letter 7 positions forward in the alphabet.
content.encoded_text: AOL MPMALS JPYJSL DHZ ULCLY TLHUA AV IL MVBUK. DL HYL AOL ZOHKVDZ AOHA RLLW AOL SPNOA OVULZA.
content.solution: THE FIFTH CIRCLE WAS NEVER MEANT TO BE FOUND. WE ARE THE SHADOWS THAT KEEP THE LIGHT HONEST.
content.hint: Shadow-shift cipher: A becomes H, B becomes I, etc. Shift of 7 positions.

content.text: Additional cipher keys, dead drop locations, and emergency protocols will be provided through your assigned speaking stone. Do not write them down. Do not share them. Do not exist.
— END OF CODEX —
[ This document will deny its own existence if questioned. ]

books.title: The Connoisseur's Companion
books.subtitle: Tea Blends, Trade Secrets, and Other Infusions
books.author: Green T (attributed)
books.description: A well-worn journal that smells of dried leaves and something faintly chemical. Tea stains cover most pages. Some recipes appear to be coded.

content.text: THE CONNOISSEUR'S COMPANION
A Guide to Refined Infusions

Tea is civilization distilled. In a single cup, you hold the labor of farmers, the wisdom of blenders, the patience of steepers, and the refined palate of centuries. To drink tea carelessly is to insult all of them.

This humble volume collects recipes gathered across decades of travel, trade, and — I confess — occasional acquisition through channels that polite society would frown upon. The Syndicate does not apologize for its methods. We apologize only for bad tea.
"A perfect cup requires perfect leaves, perfect water, perfect timing, and perfect company. Achieve three of four, and you may call yourself competent."
content.attribution: — The First Blender, founder of the Syndicate

content.text: What follows includes both legitimate recipes suitable for any tea house, and... specialized preparations that require certain ingredients not found in ordinary markets. The discerning reader will know which is which.
Chapter I
content.subtitle: The Classic Blends

content.text: very tea master must first master the foundations. These blends have sustained the Mushroom Kingdom through peace and war, celebration and mourning. They are the common tongue of the leaf.

content.title: GOLDEN SUNRISE BLEND
entries: 3 parts Fire Flower petal (dried, not fresh)
2 parts standard black leaf from the Southern Slopes
1 part crystallized Star Bit shavings
Steep at just below boiling for 4 minutes
Produces: Warm, energizing, faintly luminous amber liquid
Effects: Mild stimulant, enhanced alertness for 2-3 hours

content.text: The Golden Sunrise was Princess Peach's morning tea of choice. The palace ordered fourteen pounds of Fire Flower petals monthly to maintain supply. After the assassination, the flower farms were burned in the first wave of factional violence. The blend is now rare and expensive — a cup costs what a laborer earns in a week.

content.title: TOAD TOWN COMFORT
entries: 4 parts common brown mushroom cap (dried, powdered)
2 parts chamomile flower
1 part honey (must be from Beezo hives)
Steep at moderate heat for 6 minutes
Produces: Thick, earthy, deeply calming brown liquid
Effects: Relaxation, drowsiness, vivid dreams

content.text: The Comfort blend is what grandmothers give to frightened children after nightmares. It is also, not coincidentally, what the Syndicate gives to targets who need to sleep through certain... transactions.
The following blend is technically illegal under Iron Legion trade regulations. The Syndicate considers such regulations advisory at best.

content.title: MIDNIGHT LOTUS
entries: 2 parts black lotus flower (harvested at midnight, dried in darkness)
2 parts white lotus flower (harvested at noon, dried in sunlight)
1 part powdered moonstone
3 drops of tears (willingly given)
Steep in cold spring water for 13 hours
Produces: Colorless liquid that reflects light strangely
Effects: Clarity of thought, enhanced perception, occasional prophetic visions

content.label: [ A note has been tucked between these pages. Unfold it → ]

hidden_content.text: The Midnight Lotus recipe as written is incomplete. The REAL version requires a fourth ingredient: a single scale from a living dragon, dissolved in the moonstone powder. This is why Fawful's dragon alliance terrifies me. He has access to fresh scales. He could mass-produce Midnight Lotus. An army that sees the future cannot be defeated. — G.T.

content.text: I have seen the Midnight Lotus used three times. Twice, the drinker emerged enlightened, their purpose clarified, their path revealed. Once, the drinker emerged screaming and did not stop for six days. The tea shows truth. Not everyone can bear truth.
Chapter II
content.subtitle: Acquisition and Distribution

content.text: he finest leaves in the kingdom grow in places that do not welcome visitors. The Syndicate has spent generations cultivating relationships — and alternative access methods — to ensure supply chains remain unbroken regardless of political circumstances.
This chapter is ostensibly about trade routes. It is actually about smuggling. The distinction matters only to those who write laws and those who pay taxes. The Syndicate does neither.

factions.name: The Pipe Network
factions.description: The kingdom's warp pipe infrastructure was designed for legitimate transport. It is also, with appropriate modifications, ideal for moving cargo without inspection. A standard green pipe can be 'tuned' to open secondary channels — parallel routes that bypass official checkpoints. The Iron Legion knows these routes exist. They have not yet discovered how to close them.

factions.name: The Boo Mansions
factions.description: The Boo Aristocracy sealed their mansions during the war, but ghosts are excellent business partners. They have no use for physical goods but crave entertainment, stories, and — most importantly — the life essence that tea ceremonies generate. We provide; they provide passage through spaces that do not technically exist.

factions.name: The Koopa Underground
factions.description: Bowser's forces control the surface of the eastern territories. They do not control the tunnels beneath. Koopa dissidents — those who remember a time before endless war — maintain hidden routes through the mountains. Payment is made in medicine, information, and the occasional targeted assassination of Legion informants.

content.text: Recent events have severely disrupted our operations. The confrontation aboard the Vigilance — orchestrated, I am certain, by forces who wished to weaken all factions simultaneously — destroyed two of our primary distribution cells.

Earl Grey is dead. Exploded, specifically, after being poisoned by a dagger coated in something our alchemists cannot identify. His loss is... significant. Earl Grey managed seventeen pipe route modifications and held personal relationships with three Boo mansion lords. Replacing him will take years.

More concerning: the battle plan Remi discovered. Our assault strategy against the Onyx Hand vampire nest was SUPPOSED to be secret. The fact that a captured prisoner found it on a napkin suggests either incredible carelessness or deliberate sabotage. I have my suspicions about which.

content.label: [ Tea has been spilled across this section. Blot it to reveal hidden text → ]

hidden_content.text: Someone in the Syndicate is working with the Fifth Circle. The battle plan leak was a test — they wanted to see how we would react, who would panic, who would stay calm. I passed the test by appearing to fail. Let them think I am a fool who writes strategies on napkins. Meanwhile, I will find the traitor and serve them a very special blend. — G.T.

content.text: The Syndicate will survive. We have survived the Princess's death, the Century War, the rise of the Iron Legion, and the emergence of the Onyx Hand. We will survive this. Tea, like truth, cannot be permanently suppressed.
Chapter III
content.subtitle: Specialized Preparations

content.text: he following recipes are not tea. They are weapons, tools, and solutions to problems that cannot be solved through conventional means. Handle with appropriate caution. Test on enemies before testing on friends.

content.title: TRUTH SERUM (Gentle)
entries: Base: Strong chamomile infusion
3 parts powdered lie-detector mushroom
1 part concentrated Fire Flower essence
Administered in food or drink without target's knowledge
Effects: Compulsive honesty for 1-2 hours
Side effects: Headache, mild paranoia, occasional weeping
Antidote: Strong alcohol or sleep

content.title: FORGETTING DRAUGHT
entries: Base: Cold-steeped moonflower
2 parts Boo ectoplasm (ethically sourced if possible)
1 part powdered memory crystal
1 scale of shed Blooper skin
Effects: Target forgets last 6-24 hours depending on dose
Side effects: Confusion, déjà vu, mild existential uncertainty
Warning: Overdose causes permanent personality changes

content.text: The Forgetting Draught is why certain witnesses cannot testify. It is also why certain Syndicate members cannot remember operations that went badly wrong. We do not use it lightly. Memory is identity; to steal memory is to steal self. But sometimes, forgetting is kinder than remembering.
The following preparation is reserved for situations where all other options have failed. It has been used four times in Syndicate history. Three of those times were justified. One... was not.

content.title: THE FINAL STEEP
entries: Base: Concentrated nightshade, 13x distilled
5 parts crystallized shadow essence
3 parts Fire Flower ash (from flowers burned at midnight)
1 part powdered bone (source irrelevant)
1 drop of blood from the intended target
Effects: Death within 3-7 hours, appearing natural
No antidote exists
The target experiences a final dream of their happiest memory

content.text: The Final Steep is not murder. It is release. The target's blood ensures they are meant to receive it; the shadow essence ensures they feel no pain; the happy dream ensures they depart in peace. We offer this mercy only to those who truly deserve it.
The unauthorized use of this preparation is punishable by being served the preparation yourself. Green T makes no exceptions.

content.title: CODED RECIPE NOTATION
content.description: The following notation appears beneath the Final Steep recipe. It uses the Syndicate's trade cipher — each letter shifted by the number of letters in 'TEA' (3).
content.encoded_text: WKLV UHFLSH LV LQFRPSOHWH. WKH WUXH ILQDO VWHHS UHTXLUHV D WHDVSRRQ RI WKH WDUJHW'V UHDO QDPH.
content.solution: THIS RECIPE IS INCOMPLETE. THE TRUE FINAL STEEP REQUIRES A TEASPOON OF THE TARGET'S REAL NAME.
content.hint: Trade cipher: shift of 3 (T-E-A = 3 letters). A becomes D, etc.

content.text: Afterword
content.subtitle: On the Future of the Syndicate

content.text: I write this knowing I may not live to see the next harvest season. The events at Raventree have exposed us. The Iron Legion hunts us. The Onyx Hand suspects us. The Mages' Guild ignores us, which is somehow worse. And Fawful — Fawful has dragons.

The Tea Leaf Syndicate has endured for over a century by remaining small, flexible, and ruthlessly practical. We do not seek power; we seek profit. We do not make enemies; we make customers. This philosophy has served us well.

But the world is changing. The planar fractures at Raventree suggest that reality itself is becoming unstable. The parallel Dan entity implies that the rules we thought governed existence may be more flexible than we assumed. And the pattern that the Onyx Hand's analysts have identified — Princess, Star Road, Legion, fractures — suggests that someone has been playing a very long game indeed.

The Syndicate will adapt or perish. I am preparing contingencies. Safe houses in dimensions adjacent to our own. Alliances with entities that do not require physical form. Recipes that can be brewed with ingredients that do not exist yet but might, if reality continues to fray.
"When the world ends, someone will still want a good cup of tea. The Syndicate intends to provide."
— STEEP WISELY —

books.title: Whispers of the Star Spirits
books.subtitle: Collected Prophecies and Celestial Warnings
books.author: The Star Spirit Council (transcribed)
books.description: A crystalline tome that hums faintly when touched. The pages appear to be made of solidified starlight, and the text shifts slightly when not directly observed.

content.text: ✧ WHISPERS OF THE STAR SPIRITS ✧
Prophecies Transcribed from Celestial Communion
WARNING: This text contains information from beyond mortal comprehension.
Read at your own existential risk.

The Star Spirits do not see time as mortals do. To them, past and future are merely different angles of observation on a single, crystalline moment that encompasses all of existence. When they speak of what 'will' happen, they are describing what has always been and always will be — from their perspective.

This creates... complications. A prophecy from a Star Spirit is simultaneously a warning, a promise, and a statement of immutable fact. To hear one is to become entangled in its fulfillment. There is no safe observation distance.
"The moment you read these words, you became part of what they describe. We apologize for this. Apologies are also part of what they describe."

chapters.title: The Prophecy of the Shattered Crown

content.text: Prophecy I
content.subtitle: The Shattered Crown (Delivered 912 BF)

content.text: This prophecy was delivered to Princess Peach's grandmother, Queen Portabella, forty-three years before the assassination. It was sealed in the Royal Vault and forbidden from transcription. The seal was broken when the vault burned in 956 BF.

"The crown of mushrooms shall pass three times:
From mother to daughter in the natural way,
From daughter to darkness in a single day,
From darkness to no one — and there it stays.

The one who wears pink shall wear red at the last.
The one who guards secrets shall be secrets' grave.
The one who loves hidden shall be hidden love's cost.
The crown that is shattered cannot be saved."

The prophecy's meaning became clear only in retrospect. Queen Portabella passed the crown to her daughter, Princess Rose. Rose passed it to her daughter, Peach. Peach passed it to no one — she died without heir, and the crown was lost in the subsequent chaos.

content.label: [ The starlight here flickers urgently. Focus on it → ]

hidden_content.text: The lines about secrets and hidden love were long considered metaphorical. They are not.

Chief Thornpaw. The Rakasha leader. He was the 'hidden love.' The secret hatch in Peach's chambers — he knew about it because she showed him. She showed him because she loved him. And someone who knew about that love used it to kill her. The prophecy names the MOTIVE. — Transcriber's note, added 1040 BF

content.text: Interpretive scholars have debated the final line — 'The crown that is shattered cannot be saved' — for decades. The literal crown of the Mushroom Kingdom was never found after the assassination; it may have been stolen, hidden, or destroyed.

But some scholars argue that 'crown' refers not to the physical object but to the CONCEPT of unified rule. The Mushroom Kingdom has had no legitimate monarch for eighty-five years. Multiple factions claim authority. The 'crown' — the principle of single, consensual governance — is indeed shattered.

If this interpretation is correct, the prophecy is not merely predictive but PRESCRIPTIVE. The Star Spirits are not saying the kingdom CANNOT be reunified; they are saying it SHOULD NOT be. The shattering is intentional. The brokenness is the point.
"Some things that break were meant to break. Some shattering creates more than it destroys. The kingdom of one becomes the kingdoms of many, and from many comes... something new."
content.attribution: — Misstar, Spirit of Hope, interpreting her colleague's prophecy

content.text: The Peach Loyalists reject this interpretation violently. Their entire purpose is crown restoration. To accept that the Star Spirits INTENDED the kingdom's fracture would invalidate their cause. And so they do not accept it. Faith, as always, proves more durable than evidence.

chapters.title: The Prophecy of the Parallel Self

content.text: Prophecy II
content.subtitle: The Parallel Self (Delivered 1038 BF)

content.text: This prophecy was delivered directly to the Oracle of Raventree — two years before the Oracle's death. It was spoken in a voice that witnesses described as 'seven voices speaking one word each, overlapping into sentences.'

"There walks one who is two who is one who is none.
His name is a question; his existence is the answer.
When the cage holds the original, the copy walks free.
When the copy walks free, the cage cannot hold.

He is the crack through which light enters.
He is the crack through which light escapes.
The choice of whether to seal him or shatter him
Will determine if there is anything left to save."
content.attribution: — The Seven, speaking in unison, 1038 BF

content.text: Dan. The prophecy describes Dan the Toad.

Two years before Dan's duplication was discovered, the Star Spirits warned of its consequences. The 'cage' is the Mages' Guild null cage where the original Dan is held. The 'copy' is the parallel Dan who confessed his nature to Markop. The 'choice' — whether to kill Dan or preserve him — remains unmade.

The prophecy's central ambiguity lies in its final lines. Dan is simultaneously 'the crack through which light enters' and 'the crack through which light escapes.' He is both salvation and damnation. The choice to 'seal him or shatter him' will determine the outcome — but the prophecy does not specify WHICH choice leads to WHICH outcome.

The Mages' Guild interprets this as justification for Dan's elimination. If Dan is a crack, they argue, then cracks must be sealed. The instability he causes threatens the entire planar structure. Better to lose one toad than risk dimensional collapse.

Others — including some within the Onyx Hand's analysis division — argue the opposite. If Dan is 'the crack through which light enters,' then destroying him would eliminate the kingdom's last hope. The light that escapes may be less important than the light that enters.

content.label: [ A section of text phases in and out of visibility. Concentrate to stabilize it → ]

hidden_content.text: I have consulted with Klevar directly. He would not speak plainly — they never do — but he implied that both interpretations miss the point. The choice is not ABOUT Dan. The choice IS Dan. He must choose. He must decide whether to be the crack that lets light in or the crack that lets light out. And no one can make that choice for him. — Former Oracle, final notation

content.text: If the former Oracle's interpretation is correct, then every faction currently hunting Dan — Guild, Legion, even the Hand — is wasting their time. Dan's fate is not theirs to decide. It is his.

chapters.title: The Prophecy of the Dragon King

content.text: Prophecy III
content.subtitle: The Dragon King (Delivered 1039 BF)

content.text: This prophecy was delivered to a dying Ignis — the dragon slain by adventurers in early 1040 BF. It was recovered from her hoard by Mages' Guild operatives and has been suppressed from public distribution. This is its first transcription.

"The last great wyrm shall fall to unlikely hands,
And from her death shall rise a king of rage.
He wears no crown but fire; he commands no army but fury.
Where he walks, the world remembers it was made to burn.

Five dragons remain when the sixth lies cold.
Five dragons shall bow to the one who cannot burn.
The one who cannot burn shall burn everything,
And call it justice. And believe it. And be believed."
content.attribution: — Skolar, Spirit of Knowledge, delivered to Ignis, 1039 BF

content.text: Fawful. The 'one who cannot burn.'

How Fawful became immune to dragonfire is unknown. What is known is that he approached the five remaining dragons shortly after Ignis's death and demonstrated this immunity by walking through their combined breath attacks without so much as singeing his robes. The dragons — ancient, proud, and utterly unused to being unable to kill something — found this compelling.

The prophecy's implications are catastrophic. Fawful now commands five dragons. Each dragon can level a city. Together, they represent a military force that no faction can match. The Iron Legion's armies would be ash. The Onyx Hand's underground warrens would be tombs. The Mages' Guild's wards might hold — briefly — before being overwhelmed by sheer thermal energy.

And Fawful believes he is JUST. That is the horror at the prophecy's heart. He is not a cackling villain who knows he is evil; he is a true believer who has convinced himself that burning the world is the only way to save it. The dragons sense this conviction and find it... admirable.

events.event: Fawful appears in the Midlands, espousing revolutionary ideology
First recorded public demonstration of fire immunity
Ignis slain by adventurers — Fawful approaches remaining dragons
Alliance formalized at Fawful's victory gala

hidden_content.text: ADDENDUM — Delivered directly to this transcription:
"The Dragon King can be stopped. But only by the one who made him. Seek the fire's origin. The immunity was not earned — it was given. Find the giver, and you will find the key to Fawful's fall."

content.text: Final Warning
content.subtitle: Delivered to All Who Read This Book

content.text: You have read the prophecies. You are now entangled in their fulfillment. This is not a metaphor; it is a statement of causal fact. The Star Spirits' words do not merely describe reality — they shape it. By reading them, you have become part of their shape.
This may feel frightening. It is. The Star Spirits are not kind; they are honest. They offer truth, not comfort. And truth, as the Tea Leaf Syndicate knows, is not always bearable.

But entanglement is not imprisonment. You are part of the prophecies' fulfillment, but you are not predetermined. The future is a probability cloud, not a fixed point. Your choices matter — BECAUSE the prophecies said they would.

"The reader of prophecy becomes the writer of history. You cannot escape your role, but you can choose how to play it. Choose wisely. Choose kindly. Choose as if the Star Spirits were watching — because we always are."
content.attribution: — The Seven, in unison, to all who reach this page

content.text: ✧ MAY THE STARS GUIDE YOUR PATH ✧

chapters.title: Chronicles of the Mushroom Throne
chapters.subtitle: A Complete History of the Kingdom's Fall
chapters.author: Scribe Toadsworth the Elder
chapters.description: A thick, leather-bound tome detailing the assassination of Princess Peach and the century of civil war that followed. Marginalia in several hands suggests it has passed through many owners. The final chapters appear to have been added recently, in a hurried script.

content.text: ~CHRONICLES OF THE MUSHROOM THRONE~
A Complete History of the Kingdom's Fall
Compiled by Scribe Toadsworth the Elder
Year 1040 BF, Harvestide

To whomever finds this volume: know that what follows is not mere academic record. It is a wound given words. Every name herein belonged to a soul who breathed the mushroom-scented air of our kingdom, who walked beneath the same sun that now shines upon ruins.

I began this work in the year 1020 BF as a young scribe in the Royal Archives. Now, twenty years later, I complete it as a fugitive, writing by candlelight in rooms I dare not name. The Archives are ash. The palace is occupied. But memory endures where stone does not.
"Let the ink remember what the kingdom chooses to forget."
content.attribution: — Inscription on the Royal Scribe's Seal

content.text: Chapter I
content.subtitle: The Golden Age Before the Fall

content.text: n the years before Highsun 1, 955 BF, the Mushroom Kingdom existed in a state that later generations would regard with equal parts reverence and disbelief. The Princess ruled not through force of arms, but through an intricate web of alliances, trade agreements, and — if the more controversial historians are to be believed — genuine goodwill.

The kingdom's borders stretched from the Pipe Labyrinths in the south to the Star Road waypoints in the north. Trade caravans moved freely, protected by the Toad Guard — a civil militia more accustomed to settling disputes over market stalls than wielding weapons in anger.

Princess Peach herself was, by all surviving accounts, a ruler of remarkable complexity. The popular image — the gentle monarch in pink, eternally gracious — obscures a political mind of considerable sharpness. Palace correspondence recovered from the ruins of Toad Town reveals a leader who personally negotiated trade tariffs, who maintained a spy network that predated the Onyx Hand by decades, and who kept detailed dossiers on every noble family in the realm.

content.label: [ Examine the marginalia scrawled in the margin → ]

hidden_content.text: She also kept secrets. I found letters in the sealed vault — letters to someone she addressed only as 'T.' The handwriting trembles in places. These were not political correspondences. Chief Thornpaw of the Rakasha... he confirmed what I suspected. They were lovers. This changes EVERYTHING about the motive for her assassination. — T.E.

content.text: The economy flourished under a coin standard backed by Star Bits — crystallized fragments of celestial energy harvested from the Star Road. A single Star Bit could power a household's heating crystal for a season, making them simultaneously currency and commodity. This dual nature would later prove catastrophic when the Star Road was severed during the wars.

The Toad populace — who comprised roughly sixty percent of the kingdom's citizens — lived in relative comfort. Mushroom houses, grown rather than built, dotted the landscape in cheerful clusters. Each settlement maintained a communal garden, a message relay station connected to the capital via warp pipe, and at least one shrine to the Star Spirits.

Yet even in this golden age, shadows gathered at the margins. The Koopa Clans to the east had unified under a warlord known only as 'the Bowser' — a title, not a name, though the distinction has been lost to common usage. The Boo Aristocracy grew increasingly isolationist, sealing their mansions behind spectral barriers. And in the deep places beneath the kingdom, in caverns lit by bioluminescent fungi, something ancient stirred.

content.title: THE STAR ROAD NETWORK
entries: Seven Star Road waypoints connected major population centers
Travel between waypoints was instantaneous but required a Star Visa
The network was maintained by the Star Spirit Council
Annual Star Bit harvest provided 73% of the kingdom's energy needs
The network's destruction in 962 BF caused the 'Long Dark' — three years without reliable power

content.text: The final census before the assassination, conducted in 953 BF, recorded a kingdom of approximately 2.3 million souls. By the time the civil war ground to its exhausted conclusion eighty years later, that number had fallen below 800,000. Nearly two-thirds of a civilization, erased.
But I am getting ahead of myself. Before the blood, there was the betrayal. And before the betrayal, there was one final, perfect day.
Chapter II
content.subtitle: Highsun 1, 955 BF — The Day the Kingdom Died

content.text: he morning of Highsun 1, 955 BF began with celebrations. The Summer Solstice Festival — the kingdom's largest annual gathering — drew citizens from every province to the capital. Banners of pink and white hung from every lamppost. The smell of fire-roasted mushroom caps and Star Candy filled the streets.

Princess Peach was scheduled to address the kingdom from the balcony of the Royal Palace at the fourteenth hour. She had done so every Highsun for the previous thirty-two years of her reign. The speech was traditionally brief — a blessing, a few words of gratitude, the ceremonial lighting of the Solstice Flame.
She never reached the balcony.

At approximately the thirteenth hour and forty minutes, while the Princess was in her private chambers completing her preparations, an unknown assailant or assailants breached the Royal Suite. The method of entry remains one of the great unsolved mysteries of our age. The suite was protected by seventeen distinct magical wards, guarded by four elite Toad Guards, and accessible only through a single reinforced door.

content.label: [ A passage has been hastily glued over the original text. Carefully peel it back → ]

hidden_content.text: Seventeen wards. Four guards. One door. But Thornpaw told Mistveil about a SECRET HATCH in her room. A hatch that doesn't appear on ANY official blueprint. Someone who knew about that hatch killed her. Someone she trusted enough to show it to. The list of suspects just became very, very short. — T.E., added Highsun 10, 1040 BF

content.text: The guards were found dead at their posts, unmarked. No wounds, no poison residue, no signs of struggle. Court mages later determined they had been killed by a simultaneous cessation of all biological function — a spell so advanced that fewer than five living practitioners were believed capable of casting it.

The Princess herself was found seated at her vanity, still holding a hairbrush. A single wound — a thin blade through the base of the skull — had killed her instantly. The precision suggested either medical knowledge or supernatural guidance. No blood had been spilled on her white dress.

The body was discovered by her handmaiden, a young toad named Toadette, who had come to deliver the Solstice Crown. Toadette's scream was heard three floors below. Within minutes, the palace was in lockdown. Within hours, the kingdom was in chaos.

What followed was not grief. Grief implies a wound that can heal. What followed was an unraveling — slow at first, then catastrophic. The Princess had no heir. No designated successor. The Council of Toads, designed to advise rather than rule, found itself thrust into a role it was neither equipped nor authorized to fill.

Within a week, three separate factions had declared themselves the legitimate governing authority. Within a month, the first skirmishes broke out along provincial borders. Within a year, the Mushroom Kingdom — that gentle, golden realm of mushroom houses and Star Candy — was at war with itself.

content.title: ENCODED PASSAGE
content.description: The following passage has been encoded by the author. Each letter is shifted by 3 positions in the alphabet.
content.encoded_text: WKH DVVDVVLQ ZDV QRW DORQH. L IRXQG D VHFRQG VHW RI IRRWSULQWV LQ WKH GXVW EHQHDWK WKH KDWFK. VPDOOHU. D WRDG.
content.solution: THE ASSASSIN WAS NOT ALONE. I FOUND A SECOND SET OF FOOTPRINTS IN THE DUST BENEATH THE HATCH. SMALLER. A TOAD.
content.hint: Caesar cipher, shift of 3. A=D, B=E, C=F...

chapters.title: Chapter III: The Century of Blood

content.text: Chapter III
content.subtitle: The Century of Blood (955–1035 BF)

content.text: ar, when it comes to the Mushroom Kingdom, does not arrive as a thunderclap. It seeps in like water through cracked stone — slowly, silently, and by the time you notice, the foundations have already given way.

The first decade of conflict (955–965 BF) is remembered as the 'War of Banners,' named for the dozens of minor lords and self-proclaimed heirs who raised their own standards and declared sovereignty over patches of territory no larger than a few villages. It was almost farcical in its pettiness — mushroom farmers taking up pitchforks against mushroom farmers, each claiming their particular strain of leadership was the one the Princess would have wanted.

The second decade brought the Koopa Incursions. Warlord Bowser — or rather, the second to bear that title, the first having died of a wasting illness in 960 BF — saw opportunity in the kingdom's fracture. His armies swept through the eastern provinces with a discipline and ferocity that the squabbling toad militias could not match.

content.title: KEY EVENTS OF THE CENTURY WAR

events.event: Assassination of Princess Peach. War of Banners begins.
Star Road network destroyed. The Long Dark begins.
First Koopa Incursion. Eastern provinces fall within months.
The Boo Aristocracy seals all mansions. Thousands of refugees turned away.
Battle of Pipe Junction. Largest single engagement of the war. 40,000 casualties.
The Onyx Hand emerges as a major power broker in the underworld.
Rise of the Iron Legion. A mercenary company becomes a state.

content.text: By the midpoint of the century, the war had evolved from territorial disputes into something more ideological. Three great power blocs had crystallized from the chaos:

factions.name: The Peach Loyalists
factions.description: Those who believed the kingdom should be restored to its pre-assassination state, complete with a new monarch selected through the ancient Star Rite. They were romantics, idealists, and increasingly desperate. Their scouts — agents like Embercap and Mistveil — operated deep behind enemy lines, gathering intelligence and keeping the flame of the old kingdom alive.

factions.name: The Iron Legion
factions.description: What began as the 'Midlands Mercenary Company' in 1020 BF had, by 1035 BF, transformed into a military-industrial state. They controlled the Midlands with ruthless efficiency, taxed trade routes, and maintained the largest standing army in the region. Their motto — 'Order Through Strength' — adorned every checkpoint and garrison.

factions.name: The Onyx Hand
factions.description: Neither loyalist nor legionnaire, the Onyx Hand operated in the spaces between. Part criminal syndicate, part shadow government, they controlled the flow of information, contraband, and — it was whispered — souls. Their tribunals dispensed a rough justice that many preferred to the chaos of the surface world.

content.text: The Iron Legion's rise deserves particular attention, for it represents something unprecedented in the kingdom's history: the transformation of violence from a means into an end. The Legion did not fight for territory, ideology, or vengeance. They fought because fighting was their industry, and peace was bad for business.

content.label: [ A dried flower presses flat between these pages. Lift it to read what's beneath → ]

hidden_content.text: I write this knowing I may not survive the week. The Iron Legion has discovered that I possess copies of their internal communications — letters proving they deliberately prolonged the war by funding BOTH sides of the Battle of Pipe Junction. Forty thousand dead, and they profited from every single one. If this book survives and I do not, let these words serve as my testimony. — Toadsworth the Elder, 1038 BF

content.text: Chapter IV
content.subtitle: The Year 1040 BF — Everything Burns

content.text: s I write these final chapters, the ink still wet on some entries, I am acutely aware that I am no longer recording history. I am living it. The events of 1040 BF have unfolded with a speed and ferocity that defies the careful, measured analysis a historian owes their reader. I will do my best. Forgive the occasional trembling of the hand.

The year began with a death — as so many consequential years do. The dragon Ignis, an ancient wyrm who had laired in the northern mountains since before the founding of the kingdom, was slain by a band of adventurers. The act was celebrated by the militarists, who saw dragons as threats to be eliminated. The Mages' Guild, however, was furious.

Ignis, they argued, was not merely a dragon. She was a living repository of magical knowledge, a creature whose scales resonated with frequencies of arcane energy that modern mages could barely comprehend. Her death was not a victory — it was the burning of a library. This philosophical divide — the sword versus the staff, pragmatism versus knowledge — would come to define the conflicts of 1040 BF.
Then came the matter of Archie Miser.

Archie Miser is, depending on whom you ask, either a folk hero or a war criminal. A mage of considerable power and questionable judgment, Archie killed a fellow practitioner and was brought before an Onyx Hand tribunal — the only judicial body willing to hear the case, as the Mages' Guild demanded internal arbitration and the Loyalists had no functioning courts.
The tribunal acquitted him.
content.annotation: The acquittal of Archie Miser on Highsun 2, 1040 BF remains one of the most controversial judicial decisions in recent memory. The Onyx Hand tribunal, presided over by Judge Obsidian (a pseudonym), ruled that the killing constituted 'justifiable magical defense.' The Mages' Guild formally protested, calling the tribunal 'a puppet court run by criminals playing at justice.' Three Guild observers walked out during the verdict. One was later found dead under circumstances the Onyx Hand described as 'unrelated.'

content.text: This single decision — rendered in a basement courtroom by hooded judges whose real names may never be known — set in motion a chain of events that would see airships seized, alliances shattered, and the very fabric of reality threatened.

The airship Vigilance became the unlikely stage upon which these grand conflicts played out. Originally a cargo vessel, the Vigilance had been converted into a mobile command post by a coalition of adventurers, opportunists, and idealists who found themselves bound together by circumstance rather than choice.

The events aboard the Vigilance between Highsun 3 and Highsun 13 constitute what I have come to call the 'Thirteen Days of Chaos.' During this period, the following occurred in rapid, overlapping succession:

items.text: A smuggling ring operated by the Iron Fists was dismantled, earning the party a bounty on their heads.
An officer known only as X.O. betrayed the crew and seized control of the ship, taking Warlord Bowser himself as a captive.
The pirate Captain Syrup was freed, immediately turned hostile, and triggered a cascading series of confrontations that revealed a traitor among the toad crew.
A toad named hjumpik disabled the ship's power core with an axe — an act of either brilliant desperation or suicidal madness — sending the Vigilance into a terminal nosedive.
Over 150 trafficked toads were discovered hidden in barrels throughout the ship, each accessible only via a secret compartment opened by a Mini-Mushroom.
Archie Miser unleashed a fireball during a negotiation gone wrong, killing numerous combatants including most of the Tea Leaf Syndicate's muscle.

content.text: Each of these events, taken alone, would constitute a significant historical incident. Together, compressed into less than a fortnight, they represent a concentration of chaos that I struggle to find parallel for in the historical record.

content.label: [ The bottom of this page is stained with what appears to be tea. Tilt the page to read the watermarked text → ]

hidden_content.text: Fawful has allied with DRAGONS. After we killed Ignis, he somehow brokered a deal with the remaining wyrms. Embercap's infiltration of Fawful's gala confirmed it before everything went wrong and Jade Grit died. If Fawful can command dragonfire, no faction can stand against him. We are running out of time. — T.E.

content.text: Chapter V
content.subtitle: The Raventree Affair & The Fracturing of Reality

content.text: aventree Manor. Even the name carries weight — the kind of weight that presses down on the chest and makes breathing difficult. I visited the manor once, in my youth, before it became what it is now. It was beautiful then. A sprawling estate of dark wood and climbing roses, home to a minor noble family whose name has been deliberately struck from every record I can find.

Now Raventree is something else entirely. The manor sits at a nexus of planar fractures — tears in the fabric of reality itself — that have transformed it from a mere building into a wound in the world. Ghosts walk its halls not as metaphor but as literal fact. Rooms shift and rearrange themselves according to logics that defy cartography. The maze in the gardens is said to exist in multiple dimensions simultaneously.

It was to Raventree that the events of 1040 BF inevitably led. The Mages' Guild, the Onyx Hand, the Iron Legion, the remnants of the Tea Leaf Syndicate, independent agents, vampires, parallel-dimension duplicates, and at least one very confused plumber all converged on the manor within the span of a single week.

The reasons for this convergence are as numerous as the factions involved. The Mages' Guild sought to study — and exploit — the planar fractures. The Onyx Hand's vampire knights had established a nest within the manor, using dark crystals to sustain their undeath. The Iron Legion wanted the strategic position. And the adventurers of the Vigilance? They were simply trying to survive.

content.title: THE PARALLEL DAN PARADOX
entries: Dan the Toad exists in at least two simultaneous versions
The 'original' Dan is believed held by the Mages' Guild in a null cage
The 'parallel' Dan confessed his nature to Markop on Highsun 26
Dan's existence disrupts the Oracle's ability to function
The implications for reality stability are described as 'catastrophic'
The Mages' Guild considers Dan's elimination an acceptable cost

content.text: The events within Raventree during Highsun 26–29 deserve a volume of their own, and I suspect some future historian will provide one. For now, I will record what I can verify:

Luigi — the brother of the legendary plumber Mario, long thought to be a figure of myth — appeared at the manor on the evening of Highsun 26. His arrival coincided with an assault by Onyx knights and a series of spectral manifestations that forced several members of the party to flee through windows, off verandas, and into the nightmare maze.

Remi, the newest member of the Vigilance's crew — recruited, incredibly, after Wario handed her a box that turned out to be a bomb — found herself captured by the manor's Onyx knight garrison. During her captivity, she discovered Green T's battle plan: a frantic strategy scrawled on a linen napkin, detailing an assault to kill the vampires and destroy their sustaining crystals.

Meanwhile, Archie Miser encountered Perrius Anamatar — a being of uncertain nature and considerable power — having tea in a sitting room as though the manor were not collapsing into dimensional chaos around him. When Archie accused him of orchestrating the chaos, Perrius responded by siccing spectral coats on Luigi. Archie's counter — a massive fireball in an enclosed room — was characteristically disproportionate.
And then there was Bryan.

Bryan. A toad who arrived through a Mages' Guild portal with a single, burning purpose: to find and punish Archie Miser. Bryan called himself a servant of the toad god. He recruited Purple T for his theft skills and coerced Dan and another mage into joining his hunt. He carried divination incense that could knock a target unconscious and a faith that burned hotter than any of Archie's fireballs.
The vendetta between Bryan and Archie is personal in a way that transcends faction politics. It is, at its core, about what happens when power meets conviction — and neither is willing to yield.
Afterword
content.subtitle: Written in Haste, Harvestide 30, 1040 BF

content.text: I set down my quill knowing this chronicle is incomplete. The events at Raventree continue to unfold even as I write. Lady Aurelian Corvinarus has made her requests. The twilight grove has revealed its horrors. The Mages' Guild plots to extract the ghosts regardless of the cost to the living.

Archie was ambushed in a library — there is a bitter irony in that — and nearly killed by something the Guild has not deigned to name. He survived, though the circumstances of his rescue remain murky. A Purple Toad appeared as if from nowhere, sang a cryptic fortune-telling song, picked Archie's pockets with the casual ease of a master thief, and vanished through a portal of Archie's own making.

Reality is fracturing. The Oracle is dead. A parallel Dan walks the world while the original rots in a null cage. Vampires feast in manor halls while bureaucrats charge two thousand gold for a broken rope. And somewhere, in a sealed room that appears on no blueprint, a secret hatch holds the answer to who killed Princess Peach eighty-five years ago.

I do not know if the kingdom can be saved. I do not know if it deserves to be. What I know is that there are those who are trying — imperfect, chaotic, frequently at each other's throats — but trying nonetheless.
"The kingdom is not its borders or its crown. The kingdom is its people — stubborn, foolish, magnificent people who refuse to let the darkness have the final word."
— END OF VOLUME ONE —
[ This volume was recovered from a hollowed-out mushroom stump near the ruins of Toad Town. The author's fate is unknown. ]
